B75/M63 persist cancellation during remediation but cannot bypass remediation, restoration, verification, rollback settlement, or block release.

B71/M59, B71-P/M59-P, and B71-R/M59-R remain pairwise exclusive first-after-settlement, persisted-during-rollback continuation, and byte-identical replay paths. Their CAS rules exclude B39/M30 ordinary cleanup races.

IA16 and IA17 require work_cancel_state=NONE, so an IX01 winner excludes ordinary failure settlement by tuple-version CAS.

IA18-F adopts failure-origin FAILURE_PENDING_CLEANUP under REQUESTED, QUIESCING, or CLEANING while preserving the one IA07/IA08 CleanupManifest byte-for-byte and creating no duplicate cleanup, saga, or parent terminal.

The failure-cleanup cancellation partition remains total by attempt source, and IX03/IX04 retain sole parent cleanup/CANCELLED ownership.
Cleanup escalation cannot make DONE terminal and cannot terminal-equate secrets, credentials, live grants/leases, shared mutable workspaces, public exposure, or unclassified items.

DONE, FAILED, and CANCELLED require previously committed cleanup and settled effect/rollback/authority conditions; terminal Work is immutable, and later retained risk is handled by a separate remediation obligation or MAINTENANCE work.
